notable.note: The most significant commercial decision in this batch, and it went unremarked on the call. This prospect matches all five stated ICP criteria — owns a film production business, splits the year between Andorra and Ibiza, states outright that money is not a hardship, is a lifelong high-level athlete, and uses good-to-great language — and the rep proactively disqualified him from the $6,000 programme before ever naming its price. 'From what I'm hearing, you don't need one-on-one with Trevor... I think pitching you, working with Trevor, which is like a premium solution, it's not the right fit.' He was routed straight to the $1,000 self-paced product, so the flagship price was never spoken aloud and the prospect never got to weigh the choice. Read against the Patrick Dominguez call from the same day, where a cheaper tier existed and was withheld in order to steer a prospect up, the pattern is the same underlying behaviour in both directions: the rep decides which tier the buyer sees. The honesty here is real and worth crediting — but so is the roughly $5,000 difference. The call also surfaces two pieces of previously unrecorded information: a named head coach, Caden, who gives feedback inside the community, and a full-credit upgrade policy from Primal University into one-to-one coaching.
